title: Best Execution Policy
body:
Halcyon Ridge Capital
Best Execution Policy
Owner: Daniel Reyes, Head of Trading
Last updated: 2026-08-06
Applies to: Trading, Wealth Management, and any desk routing client or firm orders through OMS

Purpose
This policy sets out how Halcyon Ridge Capital seeks the best possible result for client orders and for orders placed on behalf of the firm. It describes the factors we weigh, how we monitor execution quality, and who is accountable. It supports our obligations under FINRA Rule 5310 and applicable SEC requirements, and it is reviewed with Compliance and Risk at least annually.

Scope
The policy covers equity and listed derivative orders, fixed income orders worked by the Sales Trading group, and wealth management orders sent to the desk for execution. Orders are captured and routed through OMS. Prices and valuations used for pre-trade checks come from PricingSvc, which is fed by MarketDataFeed. Lending and M&A Advisory activity is outside the scope of this policy.

Execution Factors
When handling an order we consider the following, in roughly this order of priority unless the client gives specific instructions:
1. Price, including price improvement relative to the prevailing NBBO or the best available quote.
2. Total cost, including commissions, fees, spread, and expected market impact.
3. Speed and likelihood of execution and settlement.
4. Order size and nature, including liquidity of the instrument and the urgency of the request.
5. Any other factor relevant to the order, such as venue reliability or information leakage risk.
For retail-sized orders, total consideration (price plus costs) is the dominant factor. For large or illiquid orders, Execution Traders may give greater weight to market impact and likelihood of completion.

Venue Selection and Routing
The Execution Traders maintain an approved venue list covering exchanges, alternative trading systems, and wholesale liquidity providers. Venues are added or removed only with sign-off from the Head of Trading and notice to Compliance. Smart order routing logic in OMS must be configured to the approved list. Any manual override of routing must be recorded in the order notes with a short rationale. Payment for order flow and rebates may not determine routing where they would conflict with the best result for the client.

Client Instructions
Where a client gives specific instructions, such as a limit price, a venue, or a time window, we execute according to those instructions, and the policy is satisfied to the extent of that instruction. Traders should flag to the client, through the relationship owner in Wealth Management, if an instruction is likely to prevent a better result on other factors.

Aggregation and Allocation
Orders may be aggregated only when it is likely to benefit each participating client or account and when allocation rules are fixed before the order is released. Partial fills are allocated pro rata unless a documented exception applies. Proprietary orders may not be given priority over client orders. Portfolio Managers using PortfolioMgr for rebalancing must submit batch orders with allocation instructions attached.

Monitoring and Review
Execution quality is monitored on three levels:
1. Real-time: Traders use TradeBlotter to monitor fills, slippage versus arrival price, and outstanding orders. Unusual slippage is escalated to the Head of Trading the same day.
2. Daily: Trading Associates review exception reports covering rejected orders, late fills, and trade-throughs, and confirm that routing overrides carry rationale notes.
3. Quarterly: The Quant Analysts produce a transaction cost analysis comparing execution results against benchmarks such as VWAP, arrival price, and venue-level fill rates. Results are presented to the Best Execution Committee.

Best Execution Committee
The committee is chaired by the Head of Trading and includes representatives from Compliance, Risk, Wealth Management, and Operations. It meets quarterly, reviews the TCA package, evaluates the venue list, and records decisions in minutes retained by Compliance. Material findings are reported to the Chief Compliance Officer and the Chief Operating Officer.

System Dependencies and Outages
Best execution relies on timely market data and pricing. If MarketDataFeed or PricingSvc is degraded, traders must confirm quote integrity against a secondary source before releasing orders and must note the condition on the order. If OMS or AuthSSO is unavailable, orders may be handled by phone only with Head of Trading approval and must be entered into OMS retroactively once service is restored. Incidents affecting execution are raised in #incidents and logged for the next committee review.

Settlement Considerations
Traders should be aware that execution choices affect settlement. Trades flow from OMS to SettlementEngine, and Operations settlements staff should be notified in advance of any unusual venue, settlement cycle, or booking arrangement.

Recordkeeping
Order tickets, routing decisions, override rationales, TCA reports, and committee minutes are retained for at least six years in accordance with firm retention standards. Records must be available to Compliance and Risk on request.

Training and Attestation
All Trading staff and Wealth Management personnel who place orders must complete best execution training on joining and annually after that, and must attest to this policy each January.

Breaches and Escalation
Suspected breaches must be reported to the Head of Trading and the Chief Compliance Officer without delay. Compliance determines whether remediation, client notice, or regulatory reporting is required. Failure to follow this policy may result in disciplinary action.

Questions
Contact Daniel Reyes in Trading or Marcus Bell in Compliance.
